data.title: Chromoblastomycosis — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 8 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Chromoblastomycosis** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. What is chromoblastomycosis and its agents?**
- Chronic subcutaneous mycosis by dematiaceous (pigmented) fungi after traumatic inoculation
- Fonsecaea pedrosoi (commonest), F. compacta, Phialophora verrucosa, Cladophialophora carrionii, Rhinocladiella aquaspersa

**Q2. What are dematiaceous fungi?**
- Fungi with melanin in their cell walls (brown/black) — also cause phaeohyphomycosis and black-grain eumycetoma

**Q3. Clinical features?**
- Slowly growing verrucous, cauliflower-like or plaque lesions on the lower limb of barefoot rural workers; 'black dots' on surface (transepidermal elimination of fungi) — best site for KOH
- Types: nodular, tumorous, verrucous, plaque, cicatricial; lymphoedema/elephantiasis, secondary infection, SCC (rare)

**Q4. What are muriform (sclerotic/Medlar) bodies?**
- Thick-walled, brown, multiseptate (septate in two planes) fungal cells resembling copper pennies — diagnostic on KOH and histopathology

**Q5. Histopathology?**
- Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, suppurative granulomas (microabscesses) with sclerotic bodies, transepidermal elimination

**Q6. Differential diagnosis of verrucous plaques (DYP favourite)?**
- TBVC, verrucous LV, sporotrichosis (fixed), mycetoma, blastomycosis, leishmaniasis, verrucous carcinoma, hypertrophic LP, iododerma, M. marinum, PEH over pyogenic infection

**Q7. Treatment?**
- Small lesions: surgical excision (wide), cryotherapy, local heat, laser
- Systemic: itraconazole 200–400 mg/day for 6–12 months or longer; terbinafine 500 mg/day; flucytosine combination; posaconazole
- Combination of systemic antifungal with cryotherapy improves cure

**Q8. In which deep mycoses is koebnerisation/autoinoculation seen?**
- Chromoblastomycosis (satellite lesions from scratching), sporotrichosis, blastomycosis

## Quick spotter facts
- Warty cauliflower plaque on the foot of a farmer with black dots — chromoblastomycosis

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Other deep fungal infections — chromoblastomycosis); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.19. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
